A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LangDriveCTRL. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original driving-video editing experiments, a 26-participant user study, component ablations and downstream object-detection results in Sections 4 and 6.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations using alternative judge models in Section 6.6, Table 12.

M1.justification: The scene-graph representation, agent pipeline, counterfactual behavior generation, trajectory refinement and video diffusion procedures are unchanged. Cycle-reconstruction training was already specified in v2 Section 3.7; v3 expands its documentation without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 30 Waymo scenes, editing tasks, grounding tests and downstream detection study. The new judge validation reassesses retained metrics, while Figure 12 adds an example of reconstruction artifacts already addressed by v2's coarse-to-refined analysis.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Cosmos, ChatSim, ChronoEdit plus Wan 2.2, Grounding SAM and 4DLangSplat in their corresponding experiments. Gemini and Claude are additional evaluators, not competing editing methods.

E3.justification: New Section 6.6 evaluates appearance alignment, collision rate and off-road rate using Gemini-2.5-Pro and Claude-Sonnet-4.6 alongside GPT-4o. This adds an evaluation protocol; the original scene selection, training settings and human-study protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a sensitivity check across judge models in Table 12 and a qualitative reconstruction-artifact removal comparison in Figure 12. Existing ablations and hallucination analyses are retained. The expanded failure discussion cites existing grounding results rather than adding another grounding experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new cross-model validation reports judge-specific percentages without adding an agreement statistic or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 12 adds Gemini and Claude scores, including 78.43% and 80.95% appearance alignment for Ours. Ours leads under every judge, although Cosmos and ChatSim reverse their appearance-alignment ordering under Claude. Existing Tables 1–11 retain their numerical results; Figure 12 adds qualitative artifact-removal evidence.

T1.justification: The scene-graph definition, counterfactual expansion and compatibility constraints, and diffusion/L2-guidance equations are unchanged, including appendix equations (1)–(10). The counterfactual mapping and compatibility tables are retained with new numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same editing capabilities, agent contributions, nearly twofold instruction-alignment claim and comparable-latency claim. The appendix additions support the existing contribution without redefining its scope.

C2.justification: Section 10 newly identifies object-grounding/localization errors as an explicit limitation and expands the explanation of traffic violations to road-structure reasoning and complex vehicle interactions. Section 9 links robustness to reconstruction artifacts with cycle-reconstruction training, and Section 6.6 discusses stability across judges.

D1.justification: v3 Section 9 explains how cycle-reconstruction training pairs are constructed: render Gaussian splats under perturbed trajectories, reconstruct another Gaussian field, then render under the original trajectory. v2 mentioned the strategy without these steps. Existing prompts, hyperparameters, hardware details and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Gemini 2.5 to support the new judge validation. Existing related-work categories, cited editing methods and research-positioning arguments remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 6.6, expands Sections 9–10, makes local grammar corrections, names GPT-4o explicitly in the metric description and improves table cross-references. Affiliations gain country names. The overall organization and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the multi-judge Table 12 and reconstruction-artifact Figure 12. Existing Figure 8 moves closer to its discussion, and appendix displays undergo local repositioning and renumbering. Existing figures and tables are retained without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Table 12 provides a useful sensitivity check for the GPT-4o-based metrics by showing that the method's lead persists under two additional judges. More explicit training-data construction and failure descriptions improve transparency. The gains are limited: judge validation uses aggregate scores, and the added reconstruction-robustness evidence is a qualitative example.
